answer: Each identity moors one buoy off a mesa headland at an inlet mouth, locking a 70-credit bond. Its ferry crosses at set speed while the buoy's lantern flashes at each crest, logging intervals by key. An auditor recomputes the interval from the wake table by speed, hull, and distance; over 3% off, a reused serial, or a shared buoy burns the bond. First buoy 34; k-th 34+6(k-1), farther moorings cost more; 1000th 6028; 1000 fakes 3,031,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-buoy ring fails: one lantern flashes one key-bound sequence, so sharing exposes both. An honest operator pays 34 once, bond kept.
